title: Diagonal Traverse of Jagged Matrix
description:
Given a 2D list of integers `nums` where each row may have a **different** positive length (a jagged matrix), return all elements of `nums` in anti-diagonal order as a 1D integer array.

Elements are ordered by increasing diagonal sum `r + c`. Within the same diagonal `r + c`, elements are ordered from the **bottom-most row to the top-most row** (decreasing `r`, equivalently increasing `c`).
hints: Iterating over the full bounding box of maxRows x maxCols wastes time on empty gaps when rows vary wildly in length.

Notice that every cell (r, c) belongs to diagonal d = r + c; if you iterate rows from bottom to top (m - 1 down to 0) and append nums[r][c] to bucket[r + c], every bucket is already in exact bottom-to-top order in O(N) total time.

examples.explanation: Even with ragged row lengths, cells sharing r + c are grouped from larger row index to smaller row index.
A single row produces its elements unchanged from left to right.
